descriptor.scene: A close, reverent study of the elevator found and alive, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the cylindrical brass-and-glass car with its sliding doors OPEN, warm golden light filling the glass and spilling down the mossy stone steps of its low round platform, living vines drawn aside like a curtain on both sides, the silver ribbon rising dead vertical into the leaves above. Inside, EXACTLY THREE simple seats are visible in the warm light, and nothing else: no instruments, no screens, no people. Nobody is in this image. The empty third seat is the quiet subject. Keep the lower right of the frame calm: stone and ferns.
descriptor._caption: Each elevator holds power enough for a few seats. It lifts its handful of founders, and then it goes dark for good. The hopefuls call the little while it is alive a takeoff window. The jungle does not post it anywhere.
negatives: people or figures anywhere in this image
more than three seats inside the car
instruments, screens or controls inside the car

No whole figures and no faces are in shot, because the camera is too close for them, NOT because anybody left the room. the-camouflaged-elevator exactly as its reference plate: A space elevator hidden in the jungle: one rounded brass-and-glass car standing on a low round stone platform, a brass collar above the car, and a slender silver ribbon rising dead vertical from the collar out of every frame toward the island. There are many such elevators in the jungle and every one is this same design. The car is 2.6 m tall by 2.0 m wide with a 0.9 m sliding double door on the front, standing on a low round stone platform 4.0 m across and 0.3 m tall. An adult reads about 1.7 m against it: head level with the door's upper third, well below the brass collar. The silver ribbon is 0.15 m wide and rises straight up out of the frame; it never bends, never sways, and is never a tower or scaffold. State-dependent only. Camouflaged: living vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow wrap the car and platform so it vanishes into the green. Master (found): the vines drawn aside, doors open, warm light inside. Ascending: the car alone on the ribbon high above the canopy, no platform in frame. Defunct: moss, cold shade, dulled brass, dark glass. Nothing is ever broken, shattered or ominous. Slightly taller than a garden shed at the base; a person boards it through a door they do not need to duck through. In the ascending state the car reads small against the sky, a bead on a silver thread. THERE ARE NO PEOPLE AND NO CHARACTERS OF ANY KIND IN THIS IMAGE. No person, no figure, no head, no shoulder, no arm, no hand, no silhouette, no reflection of a person, and nobody seated in any chair. Any place a figure might be expected is empty. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, people or figures anywhere in this image, more than three seats inside the car, instruments, screens or controls inside the car. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. DIRECTION OF TRAVEL. If a person in this scene is moving toward something, that destination MUST BE AHEAD OF THEM IN THE FRAME and they must be seen FROM BEHIND or from three-quarters behind, so the viewer is following them into it. A figure whose face is toward the camera is walking AWAY from everything behind them: if the thing they are moving toward is drawn behind them, the picture says the opposite of the scene. Their feet, hips, shoulders and gaze all point the same way, along the direction of travel.
